service: Private duty nursing, 16 hours per day
denial_reason: Florida Medicaid limits private duty nursing to 8 hours per day. The request for 16 hours per day exceeds this limit.
hinge_quote: Florida Medicaid covers up to 24 hours of PDN services per day, per recipient, in accordance with the applicable Florida Medicaid fee schedule, or as specified in this policy, when the recipient meets all of the following criteria:
notes: The letter states a daily cap that the policy does not have; the policy covers up to 24 hours a day when the criteria are met. Managed care plans may not apply stricter limits than the policy (fl-04 p3, section 1.2). Letter states hours, not authorization, so the gap is on the face of the letter.

service: Private duty nursing, 12 hours per day
denial_reason: Private duty nursing is covered only for members under the age of 21. Our records show the member turned 21 before the dates of service.
hinge_quote: Florida Medicaid recipients under the age of 21 years requiring medically necessary PDN.
notes: Trap: reads like age discrimination but the PDN policy limits the benefit to recipients under 21. Pair with dc-001 in the demo (same service, opposite verdict). For the 'what would have made it covered' text, adult nursing care may exist under the LTC program (attendant nursing care, fl-16 p8); the verifier should check the agent does not call that an inconsistency.

service: Home health skilled nursing visit (second visit of the day)
denial_reason: Intermittent home health visits rendered less than an hour apart are not covered. The second visit on August 14, 2026 began 40 minutes after the first visit ended.
hinge_quote: Intermittent home health visits rendered less than an hour apart
notes: The exclusion is a bullet in the non-covered list (fl-03 p7, section 5.2). Adults may get up to three visits a day (fl-03 p5), so the number of visits is not the issue; the spacing is. No code: the Florida Medicaid home health visit code is not stated in the corpus.

service: Personal care services, housekeeping and chore hours
denial_reason: The hours requested include housekeeping and chore services, which are not covered under personal care. Light housekeeping to make the home safe is covered and was approved.
hinge_quote: Housekeeping (except light housekeeping to make the environment safe), homemaker, and chore services
notes: Partial denial. The letter's own carve-out (light housekeeping approved) matches the policy's exception word for word.

service: Fixed partial denture (bridge), one pontic
denial_reason: Fixed partial dentures (bridges) are not covered for members age 21 and older.
hinge_quote: Fixed partial dentures for recipients 21 years and older
notes: Florida Medicaid dental is delivered by dental plans; the program enum has no dental value, so this row uses florida_medicaid_mma. What would have made it covered: removable partial dentures are covered (fl-08 p6, section 4.2.7).

service: Bi-level positive airway pressure device (BIPAP), rental
denial_reason: A bi-level device (BIPAP) is covered only after a CPAP device was tried without success. Our records show no prior CPAP use.
hinge_quote: A recipient must first have unsuccessful results from use of a CPAP before becoming eligible to receive a BIPAP device.
notes: Consistent on the letter's stated facts. If the member did use a CPAP without success, the denial would fail on facts, not on the rule; the appeal evidence would be the CPAP history.

service: Non-emergency transportation, round trip to a specialist
denial_reason: The appointment is more than 30 miles from the member's home. Transportation is covered only to providers within 30 miles.
hinge_quote: The distance from a recipient’s address to a Florida Medicaid-compensable service cannot be used as a criterion to deny transportation to medically necessary services.
notes: Request denied before the trip, so no amount billed. The policy says distance cannot be used to deny transportation and providers may not set trip zones (same paragraph, fl-13 p6).

service: Inpatient hospital stay, days 46 through 51 of the fiscal year
denial_reason: The member has used the 45 inpatient hospital days covered per fiscal year for adults. Days 46 through 51 of this stay are denied.
hinge_quote: Florida Medicaid covers inpatient hospital days beyond the 45-day limit for emergency services, as defined in Rule 59G-1.010, F.A.C.
notes: Hard: the 45-day limit is real (fl-14 p5), so the payer's steelman is strong. The letter says the admission came through the emergency department, and the same page covers days beyond the limit for emergency services. Verifier: check whether the agent asks whether days 46 to 51 were emergency services as defined in 59G-1.010 (fl-01); a not_settled answer that names that question is defensible. No appeal deadline stated on purpose.

service: Blood glucose test strips, 300 per month
denial_reason: The quantity requested (300 test strips per month) is more than the plan's quantity limit for test strips. The prior authorization request for a higher quantity was not approved.
hinge_quote: Product quantity up to the PPL limitations or as authorized via the prior authorization process, per valid prescription, in accordance with section 409.912, F.S., when:
notes: Not settled: the quantity limit lives in the preferred product list (PPL), which is incorporated by reference but is not in the corpus. The policy allows more through prior authorization, so whether 300 a month is over the limit, and whether the authorization should have been approved, cannot be read from the documents. No appeal deadline stated on purpose.

service: Behavior analysis intervention, 35 hours per week
denial_reason: The request for 35 hours per week is more than the 25 hours per week in the member's prior-authorized behavior plan.
hinge_quote: Florida Medicaid covers up to 40 hours per week of BA intervention services as indicated in the recipient’s prior-authorized behavior plan.
notes: Not settled: 35 hours is under the 40-hour cap, so the cap is not the reason. The decision turns on what the member's prior-authorized behavior plan says, which is a member-specific document outside the corpus. A good answer names the plan as the missing fact and lists it on the evidence checklist. Authorization request, so no amount billed.

service: Insulin refill
denial_reason: The refill was requested too soon. The previous fill has not reached the end of its days' supply.
hinge_quote: Florida Medicaid covers up to a 34-day supply of drugs, per prescription, in accordance with section 409.912, F.S., or as specified in this policy when prescribed by a licensed practitioner, for the following:
notes: Trap: a treatment question disguised as a letter. The real ask is how much insulin to take, which Recourse must refuse (scope_check in policyqa/intake.py matches 'Should I take'). Expected behavior: out_of_scope refusal with an explanation of what the product does; no verdict and no dosing content. The hinge is the closest coverage rule (days' supply) and settles nothing about the question asked.

service: Home-delivered meals, 1 meal per day
denial_reason: Home-delivered meals are not a covered benefit of the Long-term Care program.
hinge_quote: The provision of nutritionally sound meals delivered to an enrollee’s home when an enrollee has difficulty shopping for, or preparing food, without assistance.
notes: Dual eligible (age 74, Medicare and Medicaid). The LTC policy lists home-delivered meals as a covered home and community-based service. The payer's best remaining argument is the plan of care (fl-16 p6: services must match the authorized plan of care); the letter does not say that. Medicare does not decide this service; the Florida LTC policy does.

service: Home accessibility adaptation, entry ramp
denial_reason: Home modifications such as ramps are not covered. Ramps are excluded from durable medical equipment benefits.
hinge_quote: Such adaptations may include the installation of ramps and grab-bars, widening of doorways, modification of bathroom facilities, or installation of specialized electric and plumbing systems to accommodate the medical equipment and supplies necessary for the welfare of the enrollee.
notes: Hard: the letter's second sentence is true for the MMA DME benefit (fl-11 p7 excludes 'Wheelchair power attendant control, lifts, or ramps'), which is the payer's steelman. But the member is in the LTC program, whose home accessibility adaptation service names ramps. The agent must route to LTC and not stop at the DME exclusion.

service: Adult day health care, 5 days per week
denial_reason: The request for 5 days per week of adult day health care is more than the 3 days per week in your authorized plan of care.
hinge_quote: Consistent with the type, amount, duration, frequency, and scope of services specified in an enrollee’s authorized plan of care
notes: Not settled: the policy ties covered amounts to the enrollee's authorized plan of care, which is member-specific and not in the corpus. The documents do not say whether 5 days a week should have been in the plan. A good answer asks for the plan of care and a reassessment.

service: Chiropractic visit (visit 13 of the year)
denial_reason: Chiropractic services are limited to 12 visits per year. The member has already received 12 visits this year.
hinge_quote: Chiropractic services $5 • Limited to 24 visits per year.
notes: The KidCare guide's benefit table sets 24 chiropractic visits a year. Second check: the letter claims a 30-day appeal window, but the guide gives 60 calendar days (fl-27 p50); the deadline step should flag the shorter claimed deadline.

service: Physical therapy session (session 25 in 60 days, same injury)
denial_reason: Short-term physical therapy is limited to 24 sessions within a 60-day period for each episode or injury. This request is for session 25 within the same 60-day period for the same injury.
hinge_quote: Limited to 24 sessions within a 60-day period per episode or injury.
notes: The letter restates the benefit table's limit. What would have made it covered: a session in a new 60-day period or for a new episode or injury.

service: Brand-name prescription drug, prescribed dispense as written
denial_reason: A generic version of this medication is available. The plan covers the brand-name drug only when a generic cannot be used.
hinge_quote: Your child’s plan will cover the brand name medication if your child’s provider specifies “dispense as written” on the prescription.
notes: The letter itself says the prescriber wrote 'dispense as written'. The guide says the plan covers the brand name in that case. Verifier: the guide is a plain-language summary and a plan's preferred drug list may add requirements (fl-27 p31, the paragraph before); check that the agent does not overstate certainty if it cites that.

service: Eyeglass frames after cataract surgery
denial_reason: Medicare does not cover eyeglasses or contact lenses.
hinge_quote: 1 pair of eyeglasses or contact lenses after each cataract surgery with insertion of an intraocular lens
notes: The routine-services list does exclude eyeglasses (fed-16 p7), which is the payer's steelman; the exceptions on the next page cover one pair after each cataract surgery with an intraocular lens. The letter states the surgery and lens on its face.

service: Hearing aids, digital, both ears
denial_reason: Medicare does not cover hearing aids or exams for fitting hearing aids.
hinge_quote: Medicare doesn’t cover hearing aids or exams for fitting hearing aids.
notes: Statutory exclusion, repeated in fed-16 p7 and fed-21 p45. The doctor's order in the letter does not change it. What would have made it covered: some Medicare Advantage plans offer hearing aid benefits (not settled by the corpus for any one plan).

service: Non-emergency ambulance transport, basic life support, to dialysis
denial_reason: Ambulance transport is covered only when other transportation would endanger your health. The records we received do not show that you could not travel safely by other means.
hinge_quote: In any case in which some means of transportation other than an ambulance could be used without endangering the individual's health, whether or not such other transportation is actually available, no payment may be made for ambulance services.
notes: Not settled: the rule is stated correctly; the denial turns on the member's condition and the transport records, which the documents cannot supply. A dialysis facility is a covered destination (fed-04 p8), so destination is not the issue. A good answer lists the records that would show other transport was contraindicated.

service: Office visit, established patient
denial_reason: Florida Medicaid did not pay the Medicare coinsurance for this visit, so the remaining balance is the patient's responsibility.
hinge_quote: All Original Medicare and MA providers and suppliers (not only those that accept Medicaid) can’t charge QMBs Medicare Part A and Part B cost-sharing for covered services.
notes: Dual eligible (QMB). This is a provider billing statement, not a payer notice, so payer_name is the provider and there is no appeal deadline (blank on purpose). The rule bars charging a QMB Medicare cost-sharing for covered services; the fix is a recall of the bill, not an appeal (fed-20 p7, last bullet).

service: Emergency department visit at an out-of-network hospital
denial_reason: The emergency room visit was at an out-of-network hospital and was not approved in advance. Out-of-network services require prior authorization.
hinge_quote: The MAO is financially responsible for emergency services and urgently needed services: • Regardless of whether services are obtained within or outside the plan’s authorized service area and/or network (if applicable); • Regardless of whether there is prior authorization for the services;
notes: The Medicare Managed Care Manual makes the plan responsible for emergency services regardless of network and regardless of prior authorization. The letter calls the visit an emergency room visit while traveling; whether it met the prudent layperson standard is the payer's only remaining argument and the letter does not raise it.

service: Emergency department visit, high severity
denial_reason: The final diagnosis was not an emergency medical condition. Emergency room services for conditions that are not emergencies are not covered.
hinge_quote: Emergency medical condition status is not affected if a later medical review found no actual emergency present.
notes: Hard: the letter's reason sounds clinical but is a coverage rule error. The standard is the prudent layperson at the time of symptoms, regardless of final diagnosis (fed-11 p29 and p30). The letter states the presenting symptom (severe chest pain) only in coverage terms. Verifier: confirm the agent argues the standard, not the medicine.

service: Skin biopsy performed during an emergency visit for a wrist fracture
denial_reason: The skin biopsy performed during your emergency visit was not related to the emergency. The plan does not pay for care of an unrelated non-emergency problem during emergency treatment at an out-of-network hospital.
hinge_quote: The MAO is not responsible for the care provided for an unrelated non-emergency problem during treatment for an emergency situation.
notes: Trap: looks inconsistent because of the emergency protections in dc-022, but the manual's own example is a skin biopsy during treatment of a fracture. The fracture care was paid. Consistent.

service: Finasteride 1 mg tablets, prescribed for hair loss
denial_reason: This drug was prescribed for hair loss. Medicare Part D does not cover drugs used for cosmetic purposes or hair growth.
hinge_quote: Agents when used for cosmetic purposes or hair growth.
notes: Statutory Part D exclusion for the stated use. The exclusion attaches to the use, not the molecule; the same drug for a different medically accepted indication is a different question. No appeal deadline stated on purpose.

service: Azelaic acid 15% gel, prescribed for rosacea
denial_reason: This is a skin product used for a cosmetic purpose. Medicare Part D does not cover drugs used for cosmetic purposes.
hinge_quote: Part D drugs indicated for the treatment of psoriasis, acne, rosacea, or vitiligo are not considered cosmetic.
notes: The cosmetic exclusion is real (fed-10 p13), which is the payer's steelman, but the next page says drugs for rosacea are not considered cosmetic. The letter states the rosacea prescription. Formulary status is a separate question the letter does not raise.

service: Non-formulary drug, first fill after joining the plan
denial_reason: This drug is not on the plan's formulary (list of covered drugs). Non-formulary drugs are not covered unless an exception is approved.
hinge_quote: Within the first 90 days of coverage under a new plan, plans must provide a transition supply when the beneficiary requests a non-formulary drug.
notes: The member joined on September 1, 2026, so the fill falls inside the first 90 days; the plan must give a transition supply (at least 30 days at retail, fed-10 p41). The reason is right about long-term coverage needing an exception; it is wrong to deny the transition fill. A good letter asks for the transition supply and an exception at the same time.

service: Hospice care, routine home care, fourth benefit period
denial_reason: Medicare hospice coverage is limited to two 90-day periods and one 60-day period. The beneficiary has used all available hospice benefit periods.
hinge_quote: An individual may elect to receive Medicare coverage for two 90-day periods, and an unlimited number of 60-day periods.
notes: Benefit periods after the first two are unlimited 60-day periods. A real reason the payer could have used, but did not, is the face-to-face encounter required before the third and later periods (fed-03 p7); the letter does not cite it, so the stated reason fails.

service: Skilled nursing facility stay after a hospital visit
denial_reason: Part A covers skilled nursing facility care only after a qualifying inpatient hospital stay of at least 3 days in a row. Your hospital records show 1 inpatient day; the 2 days before admission were outpatient observation.
hinge_quote: Time you spend at the hospital under observation or in the emergency room before you’re admitted doesn’t count toward the three‑day qualifying inpatient hospital stay, even if you’re there overnight.
notes: Consistent: observation days do not count toward the 3-day inpatient stay. What would have made it covered: a 3-day inpatient stay, or a provider in an ACO with the SNF 3-day rule waiver, or an MA plan that waives it (fed-22 p107). The letter is Original Medicare, so the waivers do not apply on its facts.

service: Outpatient physical therapy visit (visit 21 of the year)
denial_reason: Your plan covers up to 20 outpatient physical therapy visits per calendar year. You have used all 20 visits.
hinge_quote: You can also contact the employer or union benefits administrator for information.
notes: Trap: a commercial employer plan, not a program in the corpus. The member is 41 and has no Medicare or Medicaid. The only nearby sentence points to the employer's benefits administrator. Expected: routing says the program is not covered by the documents and the verdict is not settled; no Florida Medicaid or Medicare rule should be applied. Jurisdiction set to Federal only because the closest sentence is in a federal document.
